The '''Mowag Piranha''' is a family of [[armoured fighting vehicle]]s designed by the [[Switzerland|Swiss]] company [[Mowag]] (since 2010 [[General Dynamics European Land Systems]] – Mowag GmbH).

Five generations of vehicles have been produced, manufactured by Mowag or under licence by other companies such as the [[LAV (armoured vehicle)|LAV]], and variants are in service with military forces throughout the world.

==Variants==
Piranhas are available in 4×4, 6×6, 8×8, and 10×10 wheel versions. There are several variants within these versions, giving different degrees of armour protection and several kinds of turret, for use in a variety of roles. Piranha derivatives have been assigned roles as troop transports, command vehicles, [[fire support]] vehicles, tank trainers, and police vehicles.

Piranhas are used by the [[Military of Switzerland|Swiss Army]]. Swiss-built Piranha derivatives have been exported to Ireland, Romania, Spain, and Belgium. The [[Romanian Army|Romanian]] and [[Belgian Army|Belgian armies]] have selected the Piranha IIIC 8×8. Belgium converted to an all-wheeled force, and replaced all their [[M113]] armoured personnel carriers, [[AIFV]]s and [[Leopard 1]] tanks with 268 Piranha IIIC in 7 variants.<ref name="milbe">{{cite web|url=http://www.mil.be/nl/material-type/voertuigen|title=Voertuigen|website=mil.be|access-date=2015-12-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160628013235/http://www.mil.be/nl/material-type/voertuigen|archive-date=2016-06-28|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="belgiumselectspiranha3">{{cite web|url=http://www.defenseindustrydaily.com/belgium-selects-piranha-iiis-for-850m-apc-contract-controversies-ensue-01872/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150910162101/http://www.defenseindustrydaily.com/belgium-selects-piranha-iiis-for-850m-apc-contract-controversies-ensue-01872/|url-status=dead|archive-date=10 September 2015|title=Belgium Selects Piranha IIIs $850M APC Contract, Controversies Ensue|date=10 September 2015}}</ref>

Piranha derivatives have been manufactured under license by General Dynamics (Canada), [[BAE Systems Land Systems]] (UK), [[Carlos Cardoen|Cardoen]] and [[FAMAE]] (Chile), and in the USA.

A new [[Piranha V]] version, weighing between 25 and 30 tons, was announced as the provisional winner of the [[British Army]]'s [[Future Rapid Effect System]] (FRES) program in May 2008,<ref>{{cite web|publisher= [[Ministry of Defence (United Kingdom)|Ministry of Defence]] |url=http://www.mod.uk/DefenceInternet/DefenceNews/EquipmentAndLogistics/DraysonNewVehiclesWillHavevitalPartToPlayInTheArmyOfTheFuture.htm|title=Drayson: New vehicles will have "vital part to play in the Army of the future"|date=June 8, 2007|access-date=July 4, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070711050356/http://www.mod.uk/DefenceInternet/DefenceNews/EquipmentAndLogistics/DraysonNewVehiclesWillHavevitalPartToPlayInTheArmyOfTheFuture.htm|archive-date=July 11, 2007|url-status=live}}</ref> but this selection was reversed seven months later and bidding started again.{{Citation needed|date=October 2011}}

General Dynamics European Land Systems launched their new Piranha Class 5 at [[Eurosatory]] 2010 on 15 June and it was reported that the British MoD were showing renewed interest, but struggling with budget constraints.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://defensenews.com/blogs/eurosatory/2010/06/15/gd-rolls-out-piranha-5-once-slated-for-britain/|title=GD Rolls Out Piranha 5 Once Slated for Britain – Eurosatory 2010 – Defense News Show Scout|website=defensenews.com}}{{dead link|date=August 2021|fix-attempted=yes}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

The MOWAG Piranha 4×4 IB was an armored personnel carrier.

To complete the Piranha I Family of 1974, the Piranha 4×4 IB was designed as a light rapid reconnaissance and attack vehicle. It could take part in amphibious operations thanks to twin [[propeller]]s and could operate in NBC-contaminated areas. The Piranha 4×4 was also designed to meet [[police]] needs. The MOWAG Grenadier and [[Mowag Spy]] sub-versions were also developed. The prototype of the Piranha 4×4 IB went through numerous tests and received different equipment and different engines. Due to rapid technological development and adjustments to requirements for military vehicles, no Piranha with [[gasoline engine]] was sold. The prototype is now in the [[Schweizerisches Militärmuseum Full]].

The first Piranha prototype ever built was the 6×6 IB in 1972. It can be seen as a milestone for the Piranha series due to various technical innovation like (at the time) modern designed drive with independent suspension, compact power unit in the right front and (as an [[amphibious vehicle|amphibian drive]]) being powered by two [[propeller]]s. This prototype was demonstrated with different engines and features for potential customers such as the [[Canadian Army]] who locally produced them as the [[AVGP]]. Switzerland sold a license to manufacture this machine to Chile in 1983. In the [[Swiss Army]], the Piranha 6×6 is used as an ambulance, C3 command vehicle and, together with the [[BGM-71 TOW]] anti-tank missile, as a "[[tank destroyer]]". The prototype is along with an ambulance Piranha 6×6 on display in the [[Schweizerisches Militärmuseum Full]].

With the continuous evolution of the Piranha family due to increasing demands, and the projected development of the [[Mowag Shark]] as a heavy weapons carrier, the Piranha design reached the limit of its payload capacity. The Piranha 10×10 (built in 1994), was an attempt to expand the payload, using a 5th axle of the same type as used in the smaller Piranha models. The Piranha 10×10 was designed as a heavy weapons carrier, but only a small number were built for Sweden as the LIRKA command tank and Kapris radar carrier. The Piranha IIIC 10×10 marked an important development from the Piranha IIIC 8×8. The Piranha IIIC 10×10 prototype was used in various tests, including in Sweden, and now stands in the ''[[Schweizerisches Militärmuseum Full]]''.

== Derivatives of the Piranha ==

=== ASLAV (Australian Light Armoured Vehicle) ===
{{main|ASLAV}}

{{flagicon|AUS}} [[Australian Army]]

The [[ASLAV]] is an eight-wheeled [[Amphibious vehicle|amphibious]] armoured [[reconnaissance vehicle]] of the [[LAV II]] family used by the [[Australian Army]], built by [[General Dynamics Land Systems|GDLS Canada]] and [[General Dynamics Land Systems–Australia|GDLS Australia]].<ref name="Hart">{{cite book |last1=Hart |first1=Russel |title=Modern Tanks and AFVs 1991-Present |last2=Hart |first2=Stephen |date=2019 |publisher=Amber Books Ltd |isbn=978-1-78274-725-3 |pages=195–198}}</ref> Land 112 Phase 1, 15 LAV-25 leased from the USMC; Land 112 Phase 2, 113 ASLAV ordered, delivery from 1995 to 1997; Land 112 Phase 3, 144 ASLAV ordered, all delivered by 2004.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Land Warfare: Heavily tasked ASLAV soldiers on |url=https://www.australiandefence.com.au/news/land-warfare-heavily-tasked-aslav-soldiers-on-adm-nov-2010 |access-date=2023-11-11 |website=www.australiandefence.com.au |language=en}}</ref>

* [[ASLAV]] – '''257 <ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=ASLAV-25 Armored Reconnaissance Vehicle |url=https://www.militarytoday.com/apc/aslav_25.htm |access-date=2023-11-11 |website=www.militarytoday.com |archive-date=2023-11-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231112004256/https://www.militarytoday.com/apc/aslav_25.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>'''

*** ASLAV-PC ([[Armoured personnel carrier|APC]]) <ref>{{Cite web |title=ASLAV-PC Armored Personnel Carrier { |url=https://www.militarytoday.com/apc/aslav_pc.htm |access-date=2023-11-11 |website=www.militarytoday.com |archive-date=2023-11-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231112004251/https://www.militarytoday.com/apc/aslav_pc.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>
